verdict.justification: Both deliverables accurately calculate the line-level Price Mismatch and Case Pack errors in Excel and build expandable outline summary tables by SKU and PO. However, Deliverable A is noticeably stronger in both its Excel summary design and its Word report. In Excel, Deliverable A sorts the summary table by Total Errors descending (starting with SKU-0107) and includes contextual metadata columns like UOM and Case Pack, whereas Deliverable B leaves the summary sorted by SKU number starting with zero-error SKUs. In the Word report, Deliverable A provides a complete table of all 10 Case Pack error lines and identifies a critical customer pattern ("Granite Small Co. accounts for 5 of the 10 Case Pack errors"), which Deliverable B misses. Finally, Deliverable B makes a minor factual error in its assumptions, claiming only three PO/SKU combinations appear on multiple lines when there are actually four (it missed PO1010/SKU-0118) and includes an awkward meta-reference to its workspace environment.

decisive_issues.issue: Factual error counting duplicate PO/SKU combinations (missed PO1010/SKU-0118, which appears in rows 35 and 36).
decisive_issues.quote: Three PO/SKU combinations appear on more than one line with different ship-to locations (e.g., PO1005/SKU-0107, PO1007/SKU-0108, PO1003/SKU-0120).

decisive_issues.issue: Includes awkward meta-commentary referencing the AI workspace environment inside a professional business memo.
decisive_issues.quote: No operative-record registry or other operations records were in the workspace folder, so the analysis rests solely on the supplied export.
